240	It was fine, we'll talk about it soon, exactly
how we will fit this together, you understand,
They already had enthusiasm,
but they cut it off, they cut off the enthusiasm. Who is the guide
of the group? An Argentinian guide from Argentina,
at all.
No religion, no law, nothing at all. Where would he
know everything?
But they saw: HaShem said to him, "Whatever
you want, go search, run away, I don't know what
you'll do. You are an independent person."
Every soul, wherever it was born, has the possibility
to go and examine
how to cling to HaShem and His Torah. True, it will be
harder for her, but she was created this way. And why?
Why was such a soul born
with this talmid chacham, this Gaon,
this tzaddik? And such a soul was born in Kibbutz Ein
Harod? Why was this soul born in Kibbutz Mizra?
It is HaShem who arranged it.
Because this soul has the strength to arrive on its own,
on its own. The soul may be lower
than the one
born to that tzaddik. Maybe it is lower,
but it was born so that you'll develop and become a tzaddik too, just as
you would have been born with him. It may be that it will be
harder than for that person there. We
don't understand; these are the ways of HaShem. In any case, the
whole purpose of the soul's creation in this world is one thing:
to know the Creator, blessed be He, to know His will, what
HaShem wants from us,
and to engage in it. And afterward, the soul, after
many long years, having passed all the trials of this
world, comes back, and they say: "Please,
here is a place, here is rest. You toiled, well done." All
the angels come and embrace her. "Wow, who are
you?" "We were created from what you did,
from your strength, from your breaking all the chains of
iron you were held in, and you went
to Torah and you went to mitzvot.
Your place is high. Please, come here, a special place,
a special rest." And the same goes for that person
who was born to this tzaddik: he also receives.
Each one receives according to the strength of his work in this world.
So the whole purpose of our work in this world is
to work on ourselves, to cling to HaShem, to cling to His Torah,
to cling to His mitzvot, after the long years. Now,
the truth is that in this world too, it is written:
The principal remains for the World to Come,
but its fruits are in this world.
Our souls receive fruits in this world, just
fruits. They give them fruits, but the principal remains. What
does it mean? What are the fruits here in this world? When you
fulfill the mitzvot and the Torah, you receive.
"How are you? Blessed be His name." What is it? He fulfilled today:
he went, he prayed today, he learned today, he
fulfilled the mitzvot, gave tzedakah, did acts of kindness, worked
faithfully. And that one went to pray Mincha, Maariv.
"What do you say?" "Yes, yes. How are you?"
"Blessed be His name. All excellent, very good, baruch HaShem."
"How are things?" "Well, they drag along." This whole world,
it's not all black. "May the whole world be destroyed, may it all burn up."
"What happened? What happened?"
These are "its fruits in this world."
These are the fruits of this world, because he
toils, you will toil.
"Man is born to toil." Who is the one who toils? One who merited the toil of
Torah, the toil of Torah, whose entire toil is
to fulfill the purpose, so that afterward,
when the soul returns, it will delight in the pleasure of HaShem. That is
the meaning, that is the whole cycle. But
generally,
people
don't have at all this thinking that we are
talking about now.
They don't have the thinking: for what were you created,
for what were you born? Tell me, what is your purpose? What
is the purpose? "I live; everyone lives, I live too;
everyone works, I work too; everyone eats,
I eat too." For what? Tell me, what is the purpose? Is it possible
to know what the purpose is? "I don't know, don't ask me
what the purpose is. I live and I eat and I
work and I get married and I have
children, and afterward, and afterward, what is the purpose?" And he dies,
and you die. The whole purpose, the whole purpose of life
is over, all of life is over. Yes, there are those
who say: "Yes, the animals too are the same, they also
live, eat and drink." "The advantage of man over the beast
is nothing."
"The advantage of man over the beast is nothing." You have nothing. What
are you? A beast? There are also beasts in the world, so for this
you were created a human and not created a beast?
HaShem created us human beings and not
beasts. For what? So that we may reach the
loftiest purpose, which is called delighting in HaShem,
to take delight in HaShem. And this is our whole purpose.
Nothing else. We toil, we are created,
we marry, we bring children, we educate them in Torah,
we educate them in fear of Heaven. All this is work.
You work, you work at how to educate the son
to be God-fearing, to keep Shabbat, to keep
prayers. This is the whole purpose, without a doubt, and then
you also receive, and he too, you educate him so that he too
will receive, so that he too will know the purpose of his
life.
So we find that the whole purpose of our lives is not just that we
live, live like everyone lives. "What do you want
from me? For what are you..."
There's a parable, in truth one should read it more
in this context. There's something I saw: there's one, Rabbi
Avraham Aram Tzova, they call him Rabbi Aram
Tzova, and he wrote a wonderful parable,
he writes, they call it
"The Train of Life."
A very beautiful parable. He says a person is born,
a person is born.
This baby is born, let's say that he is born and he
can speak, can walk, can do everything, understands everything.
